name: @swarm-hls-stream/e2e
description: End-to-end fault-injection suite that drives a deployed stack, and the unit tests that prove the harness reading it is not lying.

scripts.//test:e2e: THE && IS LOAD-BEARING, IT IS WHAT MAKES A REFUSAL STOP THE SPEND. node --test runs every file it was given even after one fails, so as a single invocation a preflight refusal printed and the scenarios then published and spent anyway, which is a checker reporting after the money is gone rather than a gate. Split in two, a preflight refusal exits non-zero before any broadcast starts. Preflight is deliberately absent from the second list so nothing runs twice. Both halves keep --test-concurrency=1 and TSX_DISABLE_CACHE=1. Note that a run now prints TWO TAP documents, so totals are summed across them and never read off one.
scripts.//test:e2e:preflight: Just the gates. Costs nothing, publishes nothing, and is the only way to check them from the deployment host, where a viewer arm actually runs.
scripts.//test:e2e:quality: One paid broadcast instead of a sitting's worth: the same gates, then V2 alone. Same && for the same reason. Exists because V2 was the one red left and re-reading it inside the full suite costs every other suite's broadcast too.
scripts.//test:e2e:vod: The same shape for V4: the gates, then the recorded-playback suite alone. One short broadcast to prove a fix to the suite without buying every other suite's broadcast.
scripts.//test:e2e:broadcast-ended: The same shape for V5: the gates, then the ended-broadcast suite alone. Same && for the same reason. V5 buys its own broadcast because the ending has to happen under a viewer who is already watching, so re-reading it inside the full suite costs every other suite's broadcast too.
scripts.//test:e2e:crash-recovery: The same shape for F: the gates, then the hard-crash suite alone. One paid broadcast to read the join the crash leaves, rather than every other suite's broadcast too. Same && for the same reason, see spend-ceiling.test.ts.
scripts.//test:e2e:batch-drain: The same shape for the drain: the gates, then scenario L alone, one rung's postage running dry on the uploader side. Deliberately absent from test:e2e, per decision 6 of docs/e2e-batch-drain-plan.md, because the ordinary full suite must never depend on a stage somebody broke on purpose. ⛔⛔ IT NEEDS AN ARMED STAGE, which is deploy/scripts/drain-stage.sh arm, and the sitting ends with drain-stage.sh restore. ⛔⛔ ONE ARMING CARRIES ONE SUITE: the depth 17 batch is spent by whichever suite fills it, and both L and V11 need a four rung ladder to lose a rung under them, so V11 has its own script below and its own arming. Settled 2026-09-04 by the orchestrator as the mechanics of the ruled decision, not a new decision.
scripts.//test:e2e:batch-drain-viewer: The same shape for V11 alone, a viewer watching through one rung losing its postage. Same armed stage requirement, same restore at the end, and a fresh arming of its own because scenario L spends the batch it fills.
scripts.//test:e2e:abr-ladder: The gates, then the ABR ladder suite alone. It exists for the end of a drain sitting: after drain-stage.sh restore has put the original batch back and redeployed, this is what proves all four rungs publish again and stay gapless. Also the cheapest way to read the ladder's shape after any change to the per-rung split, at one broadcast rather than a sitting's worth.
